reviews.text: 小心恐怖腥鹿骨，它能把你虐成二百五！ 《南瓜恐惧》：这是一款融合了生存恐怖玩法的农场经营游戏，我们需要边种地边躲怪！正是因为这种玩法它也被网友们戏称为恐怖版《星露谷》。 虽然说外号是恐怖《星露谷》，但游戏的美术风格、游戏体验和部分玩法上更像是《饥荒》的早期版本。农场内充斥着大量具有秒杀机制的怪物却没有关于它们的教程，更没有存档点。这意味着玩家需要频繁死亡重开来学习规则。小白来了进屋躲、屋子躲久了出影怪、晚上必须找小丑、绝对不要靠近鹿！当你每次因为一种新怪而死亡重开时，你势必需要调整原有的农场策略。 正因如此，该游戏在考验玩家基本的资源管理和策略规划能力的同时，还在考验玩家的耐心。游戏本身的创意和免费带来的高性价比会让各个南瓜小人愿意学习农场的生存法则，但随着时间的推移不断死亡所积累的负反馈也蠢蠢欲动，直到某一次意外死亡而彻底爆发。 游戏本身的优秀设计和正反馈过少的问题并不冲突，极低的容错率能够增加游戏的挑战性但也更容易积累负反馈，对于设计者来说这是一种两难的选择。好在游戏本身内容不算太多，如果只体验普通模式还是能够在数次死亡后”愉快“玩耍并通关的。 但噩梦模式，体验只能说糟糕。虽然本质上来说运气好一点也并非不能通关，但相对的运气不好就只能一直重开直到运气好为止。要知道《南瓜恐惧》的重复游玩价值很低，这个游戏大部分亮点都仅限于初见时期，这就导致需要频繁重开才能完成的噩梦模式和《南瓜恐惧》本身的玩法相性很差。 由于噩梦模式中怪物AI被大幅提升，这会让你时时刻刻紧绷神经，没有办法专心做自己想做的事情，对我个人来说这个模式的体验和坐牢没什么区别。整个过程我很被动而且一点错误也不能有，因为这些怪物都是秒杀机制。 最让我不满的是在这样的高压环境下，很多判定和动画却不严谨。要知道这个游戏一旦死亡就得重开，在这种程度的死亡惩罚下怎么还频繁出现判定和动画不严谨的问题?这好像是在说玩家必须谨小慎微，但作者可以马虎大意的。这无疑是不公平的！ 即便如此，我依旧推荐大家游玩《南瓜恐惧》及其噩梦模式，毕竟游戏本身设计很棒且免费，更重要的是我不能允许只有我一个人被折磨。 最新进展：作者修复了很多判定问题，且下调了游戏难度（其中包括加强部分宠物和削弱部分怪物），现在游戏十分完善，作者对这部作品是下了功夫的

一个本来三十分钟能打完的游戏，看看我的游玩时间，就因为这梦魇模式的逆天难度设计： *不给任何容错率，两只逆天鹿爹让你晚上草木皆兵，前期又没钱升级灯，你能看见鹿的时候已经可以准备料理后事了 *逆天随机位置冲过来干你的爬行怪，梦魇下tm不会有出现前提示音，速度飞快马上就到你家门口，1分半到2分钟的随机出现间隔即使用计时器掐时间也得被恶心吐，要是刷新位置和你回家相反方向等着被堵门口吧，最重量级的是出了攻击动画无论你离他多远直接因果律武器一下拍回解放前，作者真神人 *晚上小丑和爬行怪逆天无解组合技，一个要你在家隔离一个要你下楼搞核酸，只能给作者ccb了 *逆天拖时间任务不做完不让走，更逆天接任务也拖时间，乌鸦爹不给你钱就tm接不了任务，钓鱼随机出来不是任务要求更好笑 *主角体力设计更是一绝，按下奔跑啥事不干体力框框掉，能跑的时间哪怕稍微长一点点这游戏难度都不会这么离谱 *成就要求35分钟通关作者你能不能表演一个？ *能不能给种地时的司马糊脸jumpscare删了，太低级了wcsndm 我半个小时通关了普通难度，实话说挺好玩的，怪物设计简单但不乏味，种地看着钱蹭蹭上涨也有点星露谷那种爽感，虽然死亡惩罚大但普通难度设计简单合理完全值得一玩。但是到了梦魇各位阿sir还是收手吧，如上的几点已经折磨了我8个小时了，我一开始还是笑笑觉得自己太菜，后来越来越觉得奇怪，后期的死亡会给人以极强的挫败感，然后会红温，先狂骂这sm怪物设计，然后杠上了，就tm不信自己会打不过，最后备受打击放弃了，但PTSD已经形成，我现在一闭眼就能听到爬行怪跑过来的小提琴声啊啊啊 —— 我们必须想象挑战梦魇难度的西西弗斯是幸福的

Pumpkin Panic starts with an interesting concept: a roguelike farming game with horror elements, but its execution leaves much to be desired. The “first-try” mechanic, where any death or exit forces you to start over, could add tension, but instead, it feels like a punishment due to the game's repetitive and monotonous gameplay. The early minutes of each run are spent running back and forth to water crops and refill at the fountain—a tedious and uninspired loop that quickly drains the desire to restart after a failed attempt. The lack of variation in these tasks makes the replayability more of a chore than an engaging challenge. The enemies are a mixed bag. The crawler enemy is a standout, with its eerie violin cue creating a sense of urgency and requiring strategic time management. Similarly, the clowns have an interesting mechanic, with the happy clown's balloon its giving you only for you to give it back to the sad clown, following the subtle music cues, adds a simple but effective puzzle element. The shadow pumpkin, forcing you to plan purchases and movement carefully, is another creative touch that encourages strategy and balance, with a sense of tension and a reminder that nowhere is safe, and you need to escape ASAP. However, the deer is a glaring issue. This enemy feels more like a nuisance than a genuine threat. Its mechanic of requiring a wide detour or instant death upon "feeding" it is frustrating, especially when it camps outside your safe zone. This can lead to unavoidable deaths, either by the deer itself or by trapping you long enough for the shadow pumpkin or other mechanics to kill you. The deer’s slow, deliberate movements make it feel less like a part of the world and more like an arbitrary obstacle. A more nuanced design, such as two deer types with distinct behaviors or subtle signs to identify which one you have to feed, and which to stay away from, changing the pace of the game from constantly moving, to a sudden stop, this could have made this enemy more engaging. Instead, it feels lazy and unfair, soft-locking players into impossible situations far too often. While Pumpkin Panic has some creative ideas, it stumbles with its monotonous early gameplay and poorly designed challenges, particularly the deer. For a game so reliant on replayability, it needs a lot more variety and refinement to make repeated runs feel worthwhile. Right now, the experience feels more like a test of patience than an enjoyable challenge. One saving grace is the game’s price tag—or lack thereof. Making Pumpkin Panic free to play was a smart decision. A simple mistake like this in a paid game would almost certainly lead to a flood of refund requests. While I wouldn’t support the creator monetarily at this stage, given these glaring issues, I would consider it after meaningful fixes and improvements. For now, this review is based purely on my experience.

I wish there was a more "neutral" recommendation system, but I simply can't recommend this game, as it lacks basic accessibility settings. The art style is extremely pretty and I love the designs of the characters. As a concept, I also love the game, but as a disabled individual, with poor hearing, limited mobility, and vision, this game was a nightmare to play. The lack of key rebinds is a major problem for disabled people with finger related motor issues, as well as being quite rigid and in many cases difficult to use as intended. A huge issue is that a lot of the game is based on audio cues. but completely lacks any accessibility features what so ever for people with any kind of hearing/perception related disabilities. If you can't hear well, then a lot of features in the game won't work as intended, and are completely inaccessible to you. I personally found the game charming, but all of the charm is unfortunately overshadowed by a lack of accessibility options and game-play that excludes those with hearing related disabilities. For what it is, it is a great, free game, but I can't recommend it in good faith from my own experience. I understand adding accessibility features to a free game can be financially difficult, but excluding an entire group of people isn't something I can really recommend. This isn't a bad game, I think it is a great game actually. It just has some major issues that I wanted to point out.

For a free game, Pumpkin Panic was a pretty good experience. The normal mode is a very cozy horror game with a unique concept that I enjoyed a lot. Taking care of your little farm while strange things happen around you creates a nice mix of relaxing and creepy moments. It has a simple gameplay loop, but it works surprisingly well. That said, this is the kind of game that requires some hours of playtime before you really get used to everything. The more you play, the more comfortable you become with managing tasks and dealing with the dangers around you. The biggest challenge is Nightmare Mode. At first I thought it would be a fun step up in difficulty, but after several attempts it became more frustrating than enjoyable. It feels extremely punishing, and for me the amount of effort required was not worth the reward. I enjoyed the normal mode a lot more because it let the atmosphere and gameplay shine without constantly stressing me out. Overall, Pumpkin Panic is a solid free horror game with a creative idea, a cozy atmosphere, and enough challenge to keep players interested. I had a good time with it, but Nightmare Mode was where I personally drew the line. Now it's time for me to move on and play another horror game.

Came for the farming, stayed because some nightmare creature wouldn't let me leave. Pumpkin Panic somehow makes farming, fishing, and horror work together. The game is simple but surprisingly addictive. The atmosphere gets really creepy at night, and there were a few moments that genuinely caught me off guard. The only reason it's not a 10/10 is that it can get a bit repetitive after a while, and I'd love to see more content added. But for a free game, it's honestly impressive.

:sadclownface: It's a trial-and-error kind of survival mixed with progression farming (plants vs zombies maybe). So every time you make a mistake because of just not knowing what to do (your guesses won't always be right), you get to restart the whole damn tedious experience of planting and farming crops, buying upgrades, which don't affect almost anything until, perhaps, later in the game.
